In composition : (1) meaning: (a) with adjectives, it signifies usually the possession of a quality, as ἐνάλιος, ἐν́δοξος; (b) with verbs, continuance in (before ἐν) or motion into (before εἰς), as ἐμμένω, ἐμβαίνω. As frequently in Hom., absol., he (she, it), his (etc.): Act.17:28 (quoted from the poet Aratus). __2. Distributive, ὁ μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, the one . . . the other : 1Co.7:7 , Gal.4:22 ; pl., Act.14:4, 17:32 , Php.1:16 , al.; οἱ μὲν . . . ἄλλοι δέ, Mat.16:14 , Jhn.7:12 ; οἱ μεν̀ . . . ὁδέ, Heb.7:21, 23 . __3. In narration (without ὁ μὲν preceding), ὁ δέ, but he : Mat.2:14 , Mrk.1:45 , Luk.8:21 , Jhn.9:38 , al. mult. __II. As prepositive article, the , prefixed, __1. to nouns unmodified : ὁ θεός, τὸ φῶς, etc.; to abstract nouns, ἡ σοφία, etc., to pl. nouns which indicate a class, οἱ ἀλώπεκες, foxes, Mat.8:20 , al.; to an individual as representing a class, ὁ ἐργάτης, Luk.10:7; with nom. = voc. in addresses, Mat.11:26 , Jhn.19:3 , Jas.5:1 , al.; to things which pertain to one, ἡ χεῖρ, his hand , Mrk.3:1; to names of persons well known or already mentioned; usually to names of countries (originally adjectives), ἡ Ἰουδαία, etc. __2.
